items.stem: Which of the following best describes "debt distress"?
options: The abuse of entrusted power for private gain (Transparency International)
An international financial institution founded at Bretton Woods (1944) that provides loans, grants and advice to developing countries for development projects
The emigration of highly skilled and educated people from a country
A situation in which a country cannot meet its debt service obligations without major adjustment, restructuring or default
items.answer: A situation in which a country cannot meet its debt service obligations without major adjustment, restructuring or default
items.markingKey: D. "debt distress" is a situation in which a country cannot meet its debt service obligations without major adjustment, restructuring or default.

items.stem: Which of the following countries carried out "Doi Moi" reforms from 1986, combining market reforms with one-party rule?
items.answer: Vietnam
items.markingKey: C. Vietnam became one of the fastest-growing economies in Asia.

items.stem: Which of the following is the IMF's main role?
options: Lending to countries with balance-of-payments problems and monitoring the global economy
items.answer: Lending to countries with balance-of-payments problems and monitoring the global economy
items.markingKey: B. The World Bank focuses on long-term development lending.

items.stem: Briefly explain why trade rules can disadvantage developing countries.
items.answer: Agricultural subsidies in rich countries (e.g. US cotton subsidies) depress world prices, tariff escalation discourages processing, and limited bargaining power in the WTO restricts developing countries' influence over rules.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Agricultural subsidies in rich countries (e.g. US cotton subsidies) depress world prices, tariff escalation discourages processing, and limited bargaining power in the WTO restricts developing countries' influence over rules. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between export-led growth and import substitution.
items.answer: Import substitution protects domestic industry to replace imports and serve the home market (Latin America 1950s–70s); export-led growth promotes production for world markets (East Asian tigers).
items.markingKey: Import substitution protects domestic industry to replace imports and serve the home market (Latin America 1950s–70s); export-led growth promotes production for world markets (East Asian tigers). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain the difference between remittances and FDI.
items.answer: FDI is investment by firms in productive assets abroad, driven by profit; remittances are transfers from migrants to families, driven by household needs.
items.markingKey: FDI is investment by firms in productive assets abroad, driven by profit; remittances are transfers from migrants to families, driven by household needs. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Jonas writes: "Aid always leads to development." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Aid effectiveness depends on governance, design and context; poorly targeted or tied aid can create dependency and support corrupt elites, while well-designed health aid (e.g. Gavi, Global Fund) has saved millions of lives.
items.markingKey: Aid effectiveness depends on governance, design and context; poorly targeted or tied aid can create dependency and support corrupt elites, while well-designed health aid (e.g. Gavi, Global Fund) has saved millions of lives. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Kwame writes: "State-led development always leads to inefficiency and failure." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Developmental states such as South Korea and Taiwan achieved rapid growth through state guidance, though state-led strategies have also failed elsewhere (e.g. some ISI cases).
items.markingKey: Developmental states such as South Korea and Taiwan achieved rapid growth through state guidance, though state-led strategies have also failed elsewhere (e.g. some ISI cases). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly explain why remittances can be more effective than aid in reducing poverty.
items.answer: Remittances go directly to households, are spent on immediate needs (food, education, health), avoid government bureaucracy and corruption, and are larger than total ODA to low- and middle-income countries.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Remittances go directly to households, are spent on immediate needs (food, education, health), avoid government bureaucracy and corruption, and are larger than total ODA to low- and middle-income countries. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Briefly describe the 1MDB scandal in Malaysia and explain what it reveals about corruption and development.
items.answer: Billions of dollars were embezzled from a state investment fund; former prime minister Najib Razak was convicted in 2020. public funds intended for development were stolen, damaging trust and public finances
items.markingKey: Context (Billions of dollars were embezzled from a state investment fund; former prime minister Najib Razak was convicted in 2020.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: public funds intended for development were stolen, damaging trust and public finances – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to corruption and development.

items.stem: Using Ethiopia's developmental state as an example, explain state-led development in Africa.
items.answer: From the 2000s Ethiopia pursued state-led investment in infrastructure, industrial parks and the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, achieving rapid growth before conflict and debt problems after 2020. the state drove investment and growth, but political conflict and debt exposed risks of the model
items.markingKey: Context (From the 2000s Ethiopia pursued state-led investment in infrastructure, industrial parks and the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, achieving rapid growth before conflict and debt problems after 2020.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Briefly describe M-Pesa in Kenya and explain what it reveals about the role of private actors in development.
items.answer: Launched by Safaricom (partly owned by Vodafone) in 2007, the mobile-money service is used by most Kenyan adults; research found it helped lift around 2% of Kenyan households out of poverty. a technology company expanded financial inclusion, showing how private innovation can promote development
items.markingKey: Context (Launched by Safaricom (partly owned by Vodafone) in 2007, the mobile-money service is used by most Kenyan adults; research found it helped lift around 2% of Kenyan households out of poverty.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Sofia writes: "Countries with abundant natural resources always develop faster." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Many resource-rich countries suffer from the resource curse – corruption, conflict, Dutch disease and volatility – while Botswana shows good governance can avoid it.
items.markingKey: Many resource-rich countries suffer from the resource curse – corruption, conflict, Dutch disease and volatility – while Botswana shows good governance can avoid it. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Using Argentina's 2001 crisis as an example, explain criticism of neoliberal reform.
items.answer: After a decade of liberalisation, privatisation and a currency peg, Argentina defaulted on about $95 billion of debt in 2001, causing a deep recession and political turmoil. the crisis was widely cited as a failure of Washington Consensus-style policies
items.markingKey: Context (After a decade of liberalisation, privatisation and a currency peg, Argentina defaulted on about $95 billion of debt in 2001, causing a deep recession and political turmoil.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Mateo writes: "The IMF and World Bank give each member state one equal vote." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Votes are weighted by quotas/capital shares, giving the US and other large economies the largest shares; by convention the World Bank president has been American and the IMF managing director European.
items.markingKey: Votes are weighted by quotas/capital shares, giving the US and other large economies the largest shares; by convention the World Bank president has been American and the IMF managing director European. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly describe Botswana and diamonds and explain what it reveals about avoiding the resource curse through governance.
items.answer: Since independence in 1966 Botswana has used diamond revenues, managed through a joint venture with De Beers (Debswana), to fund education and infrastructure, becoming an upper-middle-income country. accountable institutions and prudent revenue management turned resource wealth into development
items.markingKey: Context (Since independence in 1966 Botswana has used diamond revenues, managed through a joint venture with De Beers (Debswana), to fund education and infrastructure, becoming an upper-middle-income country.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Outline two points that could be used to evaluate the claim: "The Beijing Consensus offers a better model of development for the Global South than the Washington Consensus."
items.answer: China's experience offers lessons on state capacity and gradualism, but it is not easily replicated, and no single model fits all.

items.stem: Evaluate the role of one MNC or NGO in the development of a country you have studied.
items.answer: E.g. Shell in Nigeria, Unilever in India, M-Pesa in Kenya, BRAC in Bangladesh; analyse benefits, costs and accountability; reach a judgement.

items.stem: To what extent is it true that good governance is the most important factor for development?
items.answer: Governance is crucial, but its effects interact with external structures; good governance is necessary but not sufficient.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: Botswana vs other resource-rich states; corruption diverts funds; Acemoglu and Robinson: inclusive institutions. items.stem: "State-led development is more effective than market-led development." Using one theoretical perspective and relevant case studies, discuss this view.
items.answer: Successful cases combine markets with a capable, disciplined state; the question is less state vs market than the quality of the state.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: East Asian tigers, China, Vietnam; market failures need state action; Washington Consensus failures (Argentina 2001).
